survey_type: codicological census (panel-by-panel), parallel in spirit to codicology_vol1-3.json's folio-by-folio watermark census
coverage: 38 physical screenfold panels x 2 painted faces = panels 1-76, following the field notebook's own panel numbering
schema_notes: Unlike codicology_vol1-3.json (watermark presence/type per folio -- a paper-based feature), Codex Borgia is a pre-Conquest deerskin screenfold and has no watermarks. Fields here are the deerskin-manuscript equivalent: support (hide joins/skin-section boundaries), condition (damage, staining, holes with measurements where recorded), grid_system (red-line/sub-grid layout), production_notes (priming, pigment, technique-sequence evidence), revision_notes (pentimenti/redrawing), tool_notes (implement identification/behaviour). Null fields mean the notebook recorded no observation for that category at that panel, not that the census confirmed its absence -- this census inherits the coverage gaps of the 2000 examination sessions rather than a fresh physical inspection. flags: 'check' = grouped/shared notebook entry where per-panel attribution is inferred rather than explicit; 'no_coverage' = panel number falls in the 1-76 range but no notebook entry was found for it in this pass -- a genuine gap, not a null result, and should be checked against the physical notebook. Panels 24, 67, 68 cross-reference technical_merged.json's original seed entries, which remain the citation-verified record for those three (used in the published festschrift essay).
